pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/execution/executions.rs:474 admits against terminal-only spend (src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/executions.rs:2346) read before the insert at executions.rs:494, so in-flight runs are invisible and a burst overshoots by up to N budgets; and src-tauri/src/engine/http_engine/openai.rs:232 stamps an unpriced remote model's run as $0.0, so that traffic spends against the cap for free

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/executions.rs:2353 reads spend on its own pooled connection and src-tauri/src/commands/execution/executions.rs:494 inserts on another - no critical section across read-decide-insert; executions.rs:2346 excludes queued/running rows so neither the candidate nor any in-flight run is counted (re-verified 2026-10-10, code unchanged since 2026-10-08)

src-tauri/engine/src/prompt/cli_args.rs:134 hands each spawn the persona's whole monthly max_budget_usd rather than remaining headroom, and the refusal at src-tauri/src/commands/execution/executions.rs:474 states neither the enforce-on-actuals mode nor the overshoot bound (carried from 2026-10-09, anchors re-read)

src-tauri/src/engine/http_engine/openai.rs:232 writes cost_usd 0.0 when price_per_million has no entry (src-tauri/src/engine/http_engine/config.rs:31 documents 'unknown models -> None, which the callers stamp as $0'; only two qwen SKUs are priced), and the remote-HTTP branch at src-tauri/src/engine/runner/mod.rs:2089 persists that zero into the summed column - nullable-never-zero broken, so an unpriced model is uncapped; the CLI fallback at src-tauri/engine/src/cost.rs:35 silently defaults unknown families to Sonnet pricing with no evidence block (estimation-announces-itself), and no unpriceable state refuses admission
src-tauri/src/commands/execution/executions.rs:474 cost x UTC calendar month x max_budget_usd x hard stop; threshold validated at src-tauri/core/src/validation/persona.rs:307 (rejects non-finite)
src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/executions.rs:2360 counts only rows WHERE persona_id = ?1, so one persona's cap cannot count or reject another's traffic
src-tauri/src/commands/execution/executions.rs:474 is a strict monthly ceiling; the technique's 'when not to use' names strict caps as hard-stop-only
src-tauri/db/src/repos/execution/executions.rs:2360 full-window SUM per admission; whether one persona's monthly row count makes the technique's 'when not to bother' hold was not measured

pairs.registryProposal: Two upward notes. (1) Restates 2026-10-09's open question: the golden path excludes an agent framework stopping its own run at a ceiling, yet this is a platform enforcing an operator-set cap over many runs it spawns; concurrent-admission and cost-evidence doctrine apply verbatim, so the precondition wording should admit the multi-run platform seat explicitly. (2) cost-evidence-and-imputation assumes ONE price book; this repo has two unaligned ones per provider path (a substring family table with a silent Sonnet default for CLI runs, an exact-SKU table with a silent $0 default for HTTP runs). A short rule on 'every engine path must reach the same unpriced-state contract' would have caught this - the technique currently reads as if one ingest seat owns pricing.
